chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Rhythm Club instrument nights and cutting out strangers
summary: At the Rhythm Club, instrument nights drew players, and newcomers who boasted were put in their place by Carter, Hodges or others.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What was it like around the rhythm club in the 1930's?
The rhythm club was one of the most fantastic places for a musician that you could ever know about.

They used to have -- When I first came to New York they used to have, one night they would have saxophone night and all the saxophone players would come in and jam. One night they would have piano night and all the piano players would come by. Then one night they'd have trombone players'

night and all the trombone players would come by and jam, you know. And if you came to town and you was a stranger in town and you thought you was great, they would -- you'd come by the rhythm club, you're going to take your horn out to play, and if you was a saxophone player and you thought you could play, they would go get Bennie Carter or Johnny Hodges to play against you and make you look bad. So don't you think you're coming to New York and take anything out, you see?

And trombones, they would get Bennie Morton or Claude Jones or when Jimmy Harrison was living or Dickie Wells to make a trombone player, a new trombone player come in, they would make him feel kind of bad, you know.

I know of a lot of trumpet players in New York that they couldn't get, Sidney de Paris Partis, Leonard Davis. They would get Rex Stewart, Bobby Stark. There was a lot of trumpet players around there then that they could get that could play.
